title: Motor show
q: A car maker, current or defunct
rule: Marques that have built cars count, whether still trading or long gone, but model names do not.

traps.Mustang: A Ford model, not a manufacturer.
traps.Fiesta: A Ford model, not a manufacturer.
traps.Beetle: A Volkswagen model, not a manufacturer.
traps.Corvette: A Chevrolet model, not a manufacturer.
traps.Harley-Davidson: Famous for motorbikes rather than cars.

fact: The Tucker 48 of 1948 had a central 'cyclops' headlight that swivelled with the steering, but only 51 were built before the company folded.

title: Scoop
rule: Flavours of ice cream, gelato or sorbet count, but brand and product names do not.

traps.Cornetto: A brand of cone, not a flavour.
traps.Magnum: A brand of ice cream bar, not a flavour.
traps.Viennetta: A branded dessert, not a flavour.
traps.Choc ice: A type of ice cream bar, not a flavour.
traps.Mr Whippy: A soft-serve brand name, not a flavour.

fact: Hokey pokey is a New Zealand classic: vanilla ice cream studded with crunchy pieces of honeycomb toffee.

title: Happy hour
rule: Named mixed drinks, hot or cold, count, but single spirits, beer and wine do not.

traps.Vodka: A single spirit, not a mixed drink.
traps.Gin: A single spirit, not a mixed drink.
traps.Tequila: A single spirit, not a mixed drink.
traps.Prosecco: A wine, not a mixed drink.
traps.Lager: A beer, not a mixed drink.

fact: The Hanky Panky was created by Ada Coleman at London's Savoy Hotel for an actor who wanted a drink with 'a bit of punch' in it.

title: Sweet tooth
q: A UK chocolate bar or sweet
rule: Confectionery brands sold in British shops, now or in the past, count.

traps.Cadbury: A manufacturer, not a bar or sweet.
traps.Nestlé: A manufacturer, not a bar or sweet.
traps.Jaffa Cakes: Sold as a cake, not a chocolate bar or sweet.
traps.Hobnob: A biscuit, not a chocolate bar or sweet.
traps.Digestive: A biscuit, not a chocolate bar or sweet.

fact: The UK's Dime bar became Daim in 2005 to match the rest of Europe; the name began as a Norwegian spelling of the American ten-cent coin.

title: Piece of cake
rule: Anything sold as a cake, gateau or traybake counts, but biscuits, pastries and puddings do not.

traps.Pavlova: A meringue dessert, not a cake.
traps.Scone: A baked bread-like treat, not a cake.
traps.Trifle: A layered pudding, not a cake.
traps.Eclair: A choux pastry, not a cake.

fact: A 1991 UK tax tribunal ruled that Jaffa Cakes are cakes, not biscuits, partly because they go hard rather than soft when stale.

title: Kitchen drawer
rule: Hand tools and small countertop gadgets count, but pots, pans, crockery and large appliances do not.

traps.Frying pan: Cookware rather than a utensil or gadget.
traps.Saucepan: Cookware rather than a utensil or gadget.
traps.Oven: A large appliance, not a utensil or gadget.
traps.Fridge: A large appliance, not a utensil or gadget.
traps.Plate: Crockery, not a utensil or gadget.

fact: A spurtle is a Scottish wooden stirrer for porridge, and the Golden Spurtle is the prize at the World Porridge Making Championship in Carrbridge.

title: Hats off
rule: Fashion and uniform headwear counts, but wigs and safety helmets do not.

traps.Helmet: Protective headgear rather than a hat.
traps.Hard hat: A safety helmet, which the rule rules out.
traps.Wig: Artificial hair rather than a hat.
traps.Crown: Royal regalia rather than a hat.
traps.Headband: A hair accessory rather than a hat.

fact: The petasos was a wide-brimmed hat of ancient Greece, and winged versions of it are worn by the messenger god Hermes in art.

title: Sole searching
rule: Specific styles count, but brand names and the catch-all word for footwear do not.

traps.Converse: A brand, not a style of footwear.
traps.Crocs: A brand, not a style of footwear.
traps.Birkenstock: A brand, not a style of footwear.
traps.Dr Martens: A brand, not a style of footwear.
traps.Shoe: The catch-all word for footwear, not a style.

fact: Emperor Caligula's nickname meant 'little boot', after the miniature soldier's caliga he wore as a child among his father's troops.

title: Bling
rule: Cut stones and organic gems used in jewellery count, but metals and lab-made stones do not.

traps.Gold: A precious metal, not a gemstone.
traps.Platinum: A precious metal, not a gemstone.
traps.Cubic zirconia: A lab-made diamond simulant, not a natural gemstone.
traps.Moissanite: Almost always lab-made, so ruled out.
traps.Glass: Man-made and not a natural gemstone.

fact: Taaffeite was the first gem identified from a cut stone rather than a rough crystal, spotted in a Dublin jeweller's tray of spinels in 1945.

title: Cut from cloth
rule: Woven, knitted and felted cloths count, natural or synthetic, but leather and plastics do not.

traps.Leather: Animal hide, not a woven or knitted cloth.
traps.Suede: A type of leather, not a cloth.
traps.Fur: Animal pelt rather than a cloth.
traps.Rubber: Not a woven, knitted or felted cloth.
traps.Paper: Not a woven, knitted or felted cloth.

fact: Qiviut, the soft underwool of the arctic musk ox, is often said to be around eight times warmer than sheep's wool and does not shrink when washed.

title: Dip in
rule: Anything served with food to add flavour counts, whether savoury or sweet, but whole dishes do not.

traps.Butter: A dairy product, not a sauce or condiment.
traps.Jam: A fruit spread, not a sauce or condiment.
traps.Marmite: A yeast-extract spread, not a sauce or condiment.
traps.Marmalade: A citrus spread, not a sauce or condiment.
traps.Maple syrup: A syrup, not a sauce or condiment.

fact: Gentleman's Relish, a spiced anchovy paste also sold as Patum Peperium, has been made to a secret recipe since 1828.

title: Fresh catch
q: A fish or seafood you can eat
rule: Edible fish and shellfish count, fresh, smoked or tinned, but dishes made from them do not.

traps.Sushi: A dish made with fish, not a fish itself.
traps.Seaweed: A sea plant, not a fish or shellfish.
traps.Fish fingers: A processed product, not a species.

fact: Bombay duck is not a duck at all but a lizardfish, usually eaten dried or fried in Mumbai.
